events.status_basis: EPA Information Quality Act response letter, dated September 18, 2026
events.summary: After an Information Quality Act correction request, EPA removed the categorical website statement that PFOA manufacture and import had been phased out in the United States and replaced it with language acknowledging that quantities of PFOA may still be produced, imported, and used by companies. This is a correction to agency wording, not a finding about any specific facility. Detection data measures occurrence; it does not establish production origin.
events.title: EPA corrects PFOA/PFOS phase-out claim after information-quality complaint

events.status_basis: Office of Water memorandum dated August 11, 2026; publicly reported September 22, 2026
events.summary: EPA rescinded its 2022 memorandum on addressing PFAS discharges through NPDES permits, pretreatment programs, and monitoring — the guidance that pushed states and wastewater utilities to use existing Clean Water Act authorities to monitor and control industrial PFAS before it reaches waterways and drinking-water supplies. This is a withdrawal of permitting and source-control guidance, not a repeal of the 4 ppt PFOA/PFOS drinking-water standards. Measured drinking-water occurrence values are unchanged; the change shifts the source-control burden toward state action.
events.title: EPA Office of Water rescinds 2022 PFAS NPDES permitting guidance

events.jurisdiction: North Carolina — DEQ and Attorney General
obligations: 2019 Consent Order obligations continue, backstopped by the $135 million reserve
events.status_basis: NC DEQ / Attorney General press release, September 10, 2026
events.summary: North Carolina announced a $590 million settlement over PFAS contamination tied to the Chemours Fayetteville Works plant — the largest environmental-damages recovery in state history. The structure: $455 million in guaranteed direct payments over 10–15 years ($380 million to 11 local governments, $75 million to the state) plus a $135 million reserve from DuPont and Corteva to support Chemours' existing 2019 consent-order obligations. Dollar amounts are a financial agreement, not a contamination measurement or a cleanup-completion metric; payment schedules and deliverables should be tracked separately.
events.title: North Carolina announces $590 million PFAS settlement with DuPont and Chemours

obligations: Required 75% reduction in PFAS reaching named waters (2019 Consent Order / 2020 Addendum)
events.status_basis: Notice issued by SELC on behalf of Cape Fear River Watch, September 23, 2026. Allegations have not been adjudicated.
events.summary: SELC notified Chemours of alleged violations of the 2019 Consent Order and 2020 Addendum, including air emissions, groundwater contamination, and continuing PFAS loading to nearby waters — alleging failure to achieve a required 75% reduction in PFAS reaching Willis Creek, Georgia Branch, Old Outfall 002, and the Cape Fear River. The notice argues the 17-compound compliance approach omits ultra-short-chain PFAS detected in finished downstream drinking water. These are allegations, not adjudicated findings; the groups say they may return to court if the alleged violations are not addressed.
events.title: SELC, for Cape Fear River Watch, alleges ongoing Chemours consent-order violations
Chemours publicly denies consent-order violation allegations
events.summary: Chemours publicly rejected the September 23 SELC/Cape Fear River Watch notice, maintaining it has not violated the 2019 Consent Order. Through a spokesperson, the company disputed the allegations and declined to address specifics. NC DEQ declined to comment on the dispute. The allegations remain unadjudicated.
events.status_basis: Chemours denial confirmed by Star News reporting (October 5, 2026; spokesperson Cassie Olszewski) and Public Radio East (September 23, 2026). Allegations remain unadjudicated.
obligations: Required 75% reduction in PFAS reaching named waters (2019 Consent Order / 2020 Addendum)

events.title: 15 states and Guam sue Corteva and Vylor over alleged fraudulent transfer of legacy DuPont PFAS liabilities
events.summary: Fifteen state attorneys general and the territory of Guam sued Corteva and Vylor in Indiana state court on October 1, 2026, alleging the spinoff of Corteva's seed business into Vylor fraudulently moved nearly $40 billion in assets beyond the reach of PFAS creditors — including the legacy liabilities Corteva inherited from the Dow-DuPont merger. The states' bid to block the separation was denied on September 30 (the Fourth Circuit reversed a freeze order and the district court declined to halt the distribution), and the spinoff completed October 1. North Carolina is not a plaintiff, but it is exposed through the September 9 settlement: DuPont and Corteva/EIDP guarantee Chemours' payments on a 71/29 basis and backstop the $135 million consent-order reserve fund. According to the companies' October 13, 2026 SEC filings, a temporary restraining order was granted on October 9, 2026, barring Corteva/EIDP and Vylor from disposing of assets outside the ordinary course, paying dividends, or repurchasing shares without court approval; on October 10, 2026, the order was stayed pending an emergency stay motion before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, so the TRO is not currently in effect. The separation itself is unaffected.
events.status_basis: Complaint filed October 1, 2026, in Indiana state court; Reuters reporting. NC exposure per the Chemours/EIDP 8-K filings on the September 9, 2026 settlement. TRO outcome per Corteva and Vylor Form 8-K filings, October 13, 2026.
obligations: DuPont/Corteva guarantee of NC settlement payments (71/29); $135 million consent-order reserve backstop

events.title: AFFF MDL notices four proposed public-water-system settlements totaling over $149 million
events.summary: The court-appointed notice administrator announced four proposed class settlements in the AFFF Products Liability MDL (D.S.C. No. 2:18-mn-2873): Carrier $129.2 million (plus applicable insurance proceeds), Archroma $14 million, Amerex $4 million, and Nation Ford Chemical $1.875 million. The settling defendants deny liability. Eligible public water systems nationwide — including NC utilities — face key deadlines: objections by November 23, 2026, opt-outs by December 22, 2026, and a final fairness hearing January 15, 2027.
events.status_basis: Simpluris (court-appointed notice administrator) announcement, October 1, 2026. Proposed class settlements, not yet finally approved.
obligations: Objections due Nov 23, 2026; opt-outs due Dec 22, 2026; final fairness hearing Jan 15, 2027

events.title: Illinois PFAS drinking-water primacy final and effective October 30, 2026
events.summary: EPA announced a tentative decision on September 30, 2026 to approve Illinois' revised public water system supervision program, finding the state adopted the federal six-PFAS rule with provisions no less stringent than the national standard (Illinois earlier set enforceable MCLs for five PFAS plus a Hazard Index mixture approach). No substantial hearing request was filed by the October 30, 2026 deadline, so under the Federal Register notice (91 FR 61847) the tentative approval became final and effective October 30, 2026 by operation of the notice — EPA issues no further notice, so finality rests on the notice's terms and the absence of a contrary filing. Illinois' standards are the state's own, mirror the 2024 federal rule, and would not automatically change if EPA finalizes its proposed MCL-rescission and compliance-extension rules. This is a comparative-state datapoint: Illinois now carries federal-alignment enforcement while North Carolina's own drinking-water rule (15A NCAC 18C .1540) sits in the legislature's tracked package.
events.status_basis: EPA Region 5 public notice (91 FR 61847), September 30, 2026: tentative approval becomes effective October 30, 2026 absent a timely substantial hearing request. No hearing request or hearing notice found in EPA, Federal Register, or Illinois sources as of November 6, 2026; Pace PFAS News & Views (November 5, 2026) reports none.

events.title: EPA's proposed GenX/PFNA/PFHxS drinking-water MCL rescission still at proposal stage — September finalization target missed
events.summary: EPA's September 2026 target for finalizing the MCL-rescission rule (GenX, PFNA, PFHxS, and the Hazard Index mixture) passed with no final rule issued. The May 20, 2026 proposal — rescinding those MCLs on procedural grounds and extending PFOA/PFOS compliance to April 2031 for qualifying systems — remains at the proposal stage. The 2024 federal MCLs remain in force during litigation; the delay extends the window in which state action (like NC's 18C .1540) carries the regulatory load.
events.status_basis: Re-verified October 14, 2026 (Pace Analytical, PFAS News and Views — October 2026): the final rescission rule remains unpublished; the D.C. Circuit heard oral argument September 18, 2026 and declined EPA's requested partial vacatur. The 2024 MCLs remain in force.

events.title: NC Ports Authority asks Army Corps to suspend Wilmington Harbor deepening over PFAS in sediment
events.summary: NC State Ports Authority Executive Director Brian Clark wrote to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on September 18, 2026, asking the Corps to suspend further consideration of the Wilmington Harbor Navigation Expansion Project — a $1.35 billion deepening of the Cape Fear River shipping channel from 42 to 47 feet over roughly 26 miles — and the associated Section 403 Letter Report activities, citing questions about PFAS contamination in harbor sediment. A record of decision is pending. The Corps said the request went to the Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works; next steps rest with OASA(CW) and Congress.
events.status_basis: NCSPA letter dated September 18, 2026; reported by WilmingtonBiz and Star News on October 5, 2026, and Public Radio East on October 7, 2026.
events.jurisdiction: North Carolina — Cape Fear River / Wilmington Harbor

events.title: Comment period closes on EPA's draft biosolids PFOA/PFOS guidance
events.summary: The public comment period closed October 5, 2026, on EPA's draft guidance for reducing risk from PFOA and PFOS in biosolids (Docket EPA-HQ-OW-2026-2509), released July 1, 2026. The voluntary guidance follows EPA's January 2025 draft risk assessment; SELC's comments argue EPA replaced that assessment with voluntary measures and urge Clean Water Act pretreatment and source control plus enforceable sludge limits instead. EPA is reviewing comments before taking next steps.
events.status_basis: EPA biosolids guidance page (public comment period ended October 5, 2026); SELC press release, October 6, 2026.

events.title: EPA launches first agency-wide PFAS TECH strategy
events.summary: EPA launched its first agency-wide PFAS strategy — PFAS Technology, Evaluation, Coordination, and Harmonization (TECH) — announced by Administrator Zeldin in Commerce City, Colorado on October 26, 2026. Over roughly two years it aims to (1) accelerate treatment and destruction R&D (foam fractionation, supercritical water oxidation, hydrothermal alkaline treatment, novel sorbents) through partnerships, (2) run pilot-scale demonstrations at Superfund sites, military facilities, wastewater plants, and drinking water systems, and (3) translate results into practice through guidance, a new Break the Bond Navigator tool, and help for water systems accessing funding and technical assistance. EPA intends grant funding for PFAS destruction research through STAR and SBIR, but announced no amounts or dates. The strategy changes no MCL and no rule; all six 2024 drinking-water limits remain in force. NC angle is context only: Morrisville-based 374Water aligned its AirSCWO technology with the strategy in October 27–29 releases — company positioning, not a regulatory action.

events.title: Environment America: PFAS detected in 25 of 29 NC waterways tested
events.summary: Environment America's PFAS report (released October 13, 2026; 2022–2024 data from the Water Quality Portal, Waterkeeper groups, and state data) found PFAS at 83% of 1,602 surface-water locations nationally. The NC-specific breakdown, published by the NC League of Conservation Voters on October 26, 2026: 25 of 29 NC waterways tested by conservation groups showed PFAS detections, 19 above 4 ppt, and 13 above 10 ppt for other PFAS including GenX. These are surface-water detections, not drinking-water compliance findings; the 4 ppt figure is the PFOA/PFOS drinking-water MCL, while the GenX/PFNA/PFHxS MCLs are 10 ppt. The report summary does not name the 29 waterways, so no county-level attribution is made.
events.status_basis: Environment America / Frontier Group report, October 13, 2026; NC League of Conservation Voters Conservation Insider Bulletin, October 26, 2026.

events.title: 3M agrees to .35 billion settlement of AFFF personal-injury claims
events.summary: 3M entered a Master Settlement Agreement on November 3, 2026 resolving the personal-injury (PI) track of the AFFF Products Liability MDL (D.S.C. No. 2:18-mn-2873): a .35 billion nominal commitment over nine years through 2034 (.8 billion present value; a .8 billion pre-tax charge in Q4 2026; a 80 million reserve for remaining and future claims is included). The opt-in deal addresses roughly 99% of current PI claims in and outside the MDL — an estimated 115,000–120,000 eligible plaintiffs — with 0 million payable in 2026, no payments in 2027, and about 20% due in the final two years. It is not an admission of liability and is subject to participation thresholds 3M may use to terminate if unmet. Judge Gergel's Case Management Orders 39 and 40 (November 4, 2026) set a November 13, 2026 deadline to identify eligible claimants and stayed PI proceedings against 3M. The deal reverses the MDL's prior posture of no PI settlement with a first PI trial expected in 2027. Claims against DuPont, Chemours, Corteva, and other defendants are not settled, and the public-water-system track is separate — the Town of Newport, NC's MDL suit, for example, is an environmental/public-water-system case and is not covered by the PI deal.
events.status_basis: 3M press release, November 3, 2026. CMO 39/40 terms as reported in MDL coverage, November 4, 2026 (secondary source; court text not independently read).
entities: U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina
obligations: Eligible claimants to be identified by November 13, 2026 (CMO 39)

events.title: EWG: final UCMR 5 data put PFAS in the tap water of 197 million people
events.summary: The Environmental Working Group's November 5, 2026 analysis of the final UCMR 5 installment — EPA's completed survey of 29 PFAS in public drinking water (final release: 1,991,977 results from 10,313 public water systems, sampled January 2023–June 2026) — estimates 197 million people are served by systems with PFAS detections, up 23 million from the prior installment, with detections at 3,595 sites and EWG's known-contaminated-sites total rising to 13,459. UCMR 5 results are occurrence and screening data: a detection, or a single result above an MCL benchmark, is not a compliance finding or a violation — compliance is judged on running annual averages under the 2024 rule. Tosson rebuilt its NC layers from the final release on November 6, 2026: the final file added 1,386 NC results, none of which raised any system's recorded maximum, so the NC figures are unchanged — 70 counties and 177 systems with detections, 47 counties above the MCL benchmark, Nash County highest at 122.5× the benchmark.
events.status_basis: EWG news release, November 5, 2026 (as syndicated); EPA UCMR 5 national summary, October 18, 2026; Tosson data pipeline rebuild against the final release, November 6, 2026.
